mission: Tess survives and retreats deeper into One Sith service. The hand learns Iresh failed and does not panic. Dorvan remains a future target, not a Book 1 puppet.
why_now: Iresh has failed and the report needs to be processed — not mourned, processed. Tess reads a debrief, adjusts the board, and accounts for the new threat profile. Skywalker's involvement changes the variables but does not change the objective.
conflict: The One Sith hand expects a failure report and receives one, cleanly, in Tess's register — which means the hand also receives the implicit assessment that Tess has already identified the next iteration. The board is cleared. The game adjusts.
setting: Coruscant, a Greyline Strategic Services secure office on a different floor than the one used at the Squeeze. Late night. Tess at his desk, alone, reading a debrief. The One Sith hand contact happens through a deniable courier channel — a single encrypted pulse on a private terminal. Tess does not gloat; he clears the board and prepares for the next move.

stakes.personal: Tess does not feel failure as failure. He categorizes it: assets used, assets lost, remaining assets, revised approach. The failure of Iresh is a data point. Talon and Skywalker are now threat-assessed at a higher tier. Dorvan remains a future objective, uncompromised, still useful.
stakes.interpersonal: The One Sith hand channel carries a single encrypted pulse. Tess reads it, composes a response, sends it. The interaction is shorter than a logistics brief. The hand is not angry. It is updating its own board.
stakes.external: The larger One Sith objective — identity-shaping techniques delivered to high-value targets — has not been abandoned because the Iresh acquisition failed. It has been deferred. The next acquisition will be approached differently, with the knowledge that Ben Skywalker will be watching.

sensory_details: Tess POV: the Greyline secure office is a different room from the one used during the Squeeze — smaller, no windows, the kind of space that looks like it was rented specifically to be forgotten. Late night. The debrief display is clean and tabular. Tess's desk has no personal objects. When the encrypted pulse arrives, the sound it makes is the same sound as any other notification.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Tess composes and sends the failure report to the One Sith hand channel — clinical, short, accurate. The response arrives within minutes: three words or fewer, acknowledgment. The hand is not disappointed. It is recalibrating.
turning_point_detail.shift: Tess reads the debrief's final section on Skywalker's actions at the Glasswell and flags two behavior patterns for the revised threat assessment: the Jacen-derived crisis clarity used in the lower basin, and the fact that the holocron container was not recovered by GA Security after the collapse. Neither fact is alarming. Both are useful.
turning_point_detail.cost: Tess closes the debrief, deletes the channel, and begins the logistics for his extraction to a Greyline affiliate site outside the Coruscant jurisdiction. The board is clear. The game continues.

emotional_arc.start: Tess reads the debrief with the same register he reads every debrief — not calm as an affect, but actually calm, because the information is what it is and responding emotionally to information is not useful.
emotional_arc.shift: The Skywalker behavior patterns flag something Tess has been waiting to assess: Ben is carrying Jacen-derived techniques that work, and he kept the container. Tess does not celebrate this. He notes it.
emotional_arc.end: Tess closes the office. He knows where the larger game is going. Dorvan is still there. The techniques are still needed. Iresh was a data point, and data points tell you what to try differently.

key_beats.beat_description: Tess alone in the Greyline secure office reads the Iresh debrief — clinical, fast, no theater.
key_beats.state_change: The failure is categorized: assets used, assets lost, remaining assets, revised approach — a closed accounting.
key_beats.pov_reaction: no pause at any item; the data moving through the same process as any other debrief

key_beats.beat_description: Tess reviews the Skywalker behavioral flags: Jacen-derived crisis clarity used in the rescue, container not recovered by official investigation.
key_beats.state_change: Skywalker's threat tier is revised upward on two specific grounds — capability and possession.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the flag logged without commentary; the second flag noted as the more operationally significant of the two

key_beats.beat_description: The One Sith hand encrypted pulse arrives; Tess composes and sends the failure report; the response is brief and recalibrating, not punishing.
key_beats.state_change: The hand acknowledges the failure as a data point and adjusts its own board — the objective is deferred, not abandoned.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the response read and closed; the brevity of the hand's reply consistent with its prior communications

key_beats.beat_description: Tess flags Dorvan's status as unchanged — future target, not yet compromised, still useful.
key_beats.state_change: The long-range objective survives the Iresh failure intact; the next iteration will have the benefit of a revised Skywalker threat assessment.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the entry made without emphasis; a variable that has not moved is noted as such

key_beats.beat_description: Tess begins extraction logistics, clears the secure office, and deletes the channel.
key_beats.state_change: His presence in the Coruscant jurisdiction ends; the game moves to its next configuration.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the familiar sequence of closing an operation; each step the same as every prior extraction
